Senses.Explanation: A water buffalo, repeatedly put to work in Chan speech and cases. Guishan says that after death he will become one bearing his monastic name; Da'an describes watching, restraining, and gradually taming one until it becomes the white ox in the open field; and Zhaozhou calls Hanshan and Shide two water buffaloes. Nanquan likewise says that Old Teacher Wang has raised a water buffalo, and answers a question about where a person who knows-there-is goes by saying that he becomes one at a patron's house. In the joined exchange Nanquan then says that people must go among the different kinds and responds to a question about the kinds by putting both hands on the ground. These are distinct recorded deployments of the same animal referent, not a separate Nanquan thing or an interpretive buffalo-as-self sense.
Senses.Note: The headword has 1,076 hits in 257 allowlisted texts. The corpus-wide animal remains one referent across ox-herding, a posthumous buffalo declaration, teasing, public questions, and case allusions. Nanquan's lines are retained as especially important deployments, but neither the person who knows-there-is (知有底人) nor going among the different kinds (異類中行) provides a corpus definition that changes the buffalo into a second thing. The floating Da'an/Nanquan attribution of the ox-herding line is preserved in its occurrence note rather than used to manufacture a Nanquan-owned sense.

Occurrences.Kwic: 老僧百年後。向山下作一頭水牯牛。左脇下書五字。曰。溈山僧某甲。當恁麼時。喚作溈山僧又是水牯牛。喚作水牯牛又是溈山僧。畢竟喚作甚麼即得。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), Guishan Lingyou section: Guishan Lingyou says that after his death he will become a water buffalo bearing his monastic name and publicly asks what it should be called.

Occurrences.Kwic: 只看一頭水牯牛。若落路入草便牽出。若犯人苗稼即鞭撻調伏。既久可憐生受人言語。如今變作箇露地白牛常在面前。終日露逈逈地。趁亦不去也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄), Changqing Da'an section: Changqing Da'an is the speaker of this stored oxherding line. A parallel later in the same source introduces the wording as 'Nanquan said,' so the transmission attribution floats; this occurrence remains assigned to its exact section speaker.
Recorded Sayings of Master Zhaozhou (趙州和尚語錄): Zhaozhou Congshen is the exact speaker who says that on arriving he saw only two water buffaloes, referring to Hanshan and Shide.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂曰。王老師自小養一頭水牯牛。擬向溪東牧。不免食他國王水草。擬向溪西牧。亦不免食他國王水草。不如隨分納些些。總不見得。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), Nanquan Puyuan section: Nanquan Puyuan uses his self-name Old Teacher Wang and says that he has raised a water buffalo.

Occurrences.Kwic: 知有底人向甚麼處去。泉曰。山前檀越家作一頭水牯牛去。師曰。謝師指示。泉曰。昨夜三更月到牕。泉曰。今時人。須向異類中行始得。師曰。異即不問。如何是類。泉以兩手拓地。師近前一踏。踏倒。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元): Nanquan Puyuan is the exact respondent who says the person who knows-there-is becomes a water buffalo at a patron's house, then continues the joined exchange about going among the different kinds.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師問南泉：「知有底人向什麼處去？」泉云：「山前檀越家作一頭水牯牛去。」師云：「謝和尚指示。」泉云：「昨夜三更月到窗。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Master Zhaozhou (趙州和尚語錄): the record independently preserves Nanquan Puyuan's exact answer that the person who knows-there-is becomes a water buffalo at a patron's house.

Occurrences.Kwic: 所以古人權借水牯牛為異類。秖是事上異類。非言語中異類。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Caoshan Yuanzheng of Fuzhou (撫州曹山元證禪師語錄): Caoshan Benji explicitly says that the ancients provisionally borrowed the water buffalo for the different kind and distinguishes the kind-in-fact from the kind-in-words.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云水牯牛安樂麼僧云及時水草師云為什麼傷人苗稼僧云對和尚不敢造次
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄): Shoushan Xingnian asks an unnamed monk whether the water buffalo is at ease; the monk answers and Shoushan continues the test.
